subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Should OpenClaw decouple Telegram runner sink concurrency from agents.defaults.maxConcurrent for multi-agent Telegram deployments, or keep the current shared concurrency model and document/tune the supported operator settings?
rationale: The remaining code-backed gap is not just a local defect: it changes how channel ingress competes with agent turn concurrency and could affect delivery ordering, resource use, and operator expectations.

options.title: Decouple Telegram ingress concurrency
options.body: Add a narrow Telegram-owned concurrency setting or derived default, with live Telegram proof and regression coverage for polling delivery under concurrent agent load.

options.title: Keep shared concurrency
options.body: Leave sink.concurrency tied to agent maxConcurrent and update diagnostics/docs to steer operators toward supported provider timeout and process-level tuning.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Hold code changes until a current-main trace proves whether Telegram ingress, provider transport, auth cooldown, or local runtime coordination is the remaining bottleneck.

recommendation.title: Decouple Telegram ingress concurrency
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Telegram-owned concurrency setting or derived default, with live Telegram proof and regression coverage for polling delivery under concurrent agent load.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged terminal-abort work is the closest concrete ownership trail for the fallback cascade side, though the Telegram concurrency decision may need a channel owner as well.
